sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Sector breadth is extremely narrow with only Technology posting an all-green profile, while Energy and Technology dominate relative momentum across the market.

Market leadership remains heavily concentrated at the top. Technology stands out as the lone sector sustaining multi-timeframe positive momentum (0.950), backed by top-3 consistency over 1, 3, and 6 months. Energy maintains the top YTD rank with strong momentum (0.833), followed by Industrials (0.617) and Healthcare (0.567). 

Short-term rotation has completely stalled, with no sectors shifting rank positions over the past 5 sessions. Defensive and interest-rate-sensitive pockets continue to fade at the bottom of the board, with Utilities (0.217) and Real Estate (0.233) lagging the broader market alongside weak performance in Consumer Cyclical (0.333) and Consumer Defensive (0.333).

## Strength
- **Narrow leadership:** Only 1 of 11 sectors (Technology) is all-green across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes.
- **Sustained outperformance:** Technology holds a 0.950 momentum score (rank 2 YTD) and remains the only group maintaining sustained top-3 status across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- **YTD front-runner:** Energy holds the #1 YTD rank with an elevated momentum score of 0.833.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Frozen ranks:** All tracked sectors recorded 0 rank movement over the last 5 sessions, signaling zero relative position changes across the board.
- **Momentum top tier:** Technology (0.950), Energy (0.833), and Industrials (0.617, rank 4 YTD) lead the market in relative strength.
- **Deep laggards:** Utilities (0.217, rank 10 YTD) and Real Estate (0.233, rank 8 YTD) represent the absolute bottom of momentum rankings, trailed closely by Consumer Cyclical (0.333, rank 11 YTD).

## Divergences
- **Communication Services rank mismatch:** Communication Services carries mid-tier momentum (0.550) despite a weak #9 YTD rank.
- **Consumer Defensive lag:** Consumer Defensive sits at a low 0.333 momentum score despite holding a mid-pack YTD rank of 6.
- **No fragile leaders:** No sectors currently meet the criteria for fragile all-green status, leaving Technology's leadership fully uncontested and uncompromised.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Broad-market leadership remains tightly concentrated in just 8 all-green industries led by refining and tech hardware, while short-term rotation favors distribution and logistics over precious metals and financials.

Leadership continues to be anchored by energy and technology supply chains. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.981) and Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.980) command the market alongside Semiconductors (0.946) and Marine Shipping (0.938), all maintaining sustained outperformance across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons. 

Shorter-term capital is rotating into supply chain and logistics plays, with Medical Distribution jumping 14 spots to rank 62 and Integrated Freight & Logistics gaining 13 spots to rank 56. Conversely, sharp pullbacks hit precious metals and financial groups, as Gold plunged 15 spots to rank 67 and Capital Markets slid 11 spots to rank 70.

## Strength
- **Narrow all-green breadth:** Only 8 of 144 groups are positive across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, YTD), led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.98 momentum), Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.98), and Semiconductors (0.95).
- **Persistent leaders:** Sustained top-36 ranks across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month windows are held by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, Electronics & Computer Distribution, Semiconductors, Marine Shipping, Communication Equipment, Scientific & Technical Instruments, Copper, and Computer Hardware.
- **Top momentum scores:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.981, rank_ytd 2) and Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.980, rank_ytd 3) hold the highest absolute momentum across all industries.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Logistics and distribution advancing:** Top 5-session gainers include Medical Distribution (+14 spots to rank 62, momentum 0.69), Integrated Freight & Logistics (+13 spots to rank 56, momentum 0.56), and Trucking (+12 spots to rank 21, momentum 0.68).
- **Metals and financials sliding:** Major 5-session rank drops hit Gold (-15 spots to rank 67, momentum 0.44), Other Precious Metals & Mining (-12 spots to rank 111, momentum 0.31), and Capital Markets (-11 spots to rank 70, momentum 0.43).
- **Entrenched laggards:** Consumer-facing services and mortgage groups anchor the bottom ranks, with Gambling (momentum 0.016, rank_ytd 143), Advertising Agencies (0.022, rank_ytd 144), and Mortgage Finance (0.036, rank_ytd 142) posting negligible momentum.

## Divergences
- **Fading strength:** High-momentum groups showing near-term deterioration include Diagnostics & Research (momentum 0.78, rank down 5 spots), Consumer Electronics (momentum 0.79, rank down 2 spots), and Steel (momentum 0.70, rank down 3 spots).
- **Emerging bottom turnarounds:** Rapid 5-session rank improvements are appearing in low-momentum industries, specifically Luxury Goods (+13 spots, momentum 0.47), Grocery Stores (+7 spots, momentum 0.43), and Restaurants (+7 spots, momentum 0.27).
